svg.aria-label: Scenario 2, defense rehearsal. You ask: My defense is in two weeks — drill me. Everything happens in your session; no role in this flow is dispatched, because results-analyst, science-presenter and study-coach are all shared-context skills. Step 1, /research-master:results-analyst gives verified numbers and figures: tables and figures, each from a committed script named in the output, and the primary metric with its spread, mean ± sample sd across folds (and seeds when multi-seed), never a lone number; it never massages a number, and unflattering metrics are reported as found. Step 2, /research-master:science-presenter does brief, pre-flight scan and build: the brief is blocking, before any design work (audience and venue, time limit, language), every source is verified on disk before anything is embedded, and it returns the deck and backup-math slides; the defense / viva preset (mixed, will probe) puts claims with backup-math slides behind each. It never computes a new statistic and never skips the brief; a missing number is a request to /results-analyst, which goes back through you. Step 3, for a defense, /research-master:study-coach rehearses: it reads the Study Log first, then teaches one topic in three layers, intuition, formalism and defense phrasing, the last being 2–3 sentences you could say to an examiner, stopping after each layer for your go-ahead, and before moving up you explain each layer back; then a quiz of 3–5 questions, today's topic plus exactly one from the weak-spot queue, graded honestly. It never verifies, builds or presents; it teaches only. Step 4, the Study Log is updated: a session row with date, topic and quiz result, curriculum boxes ticked, weak spots added or retired, Next up set; a wrong answer is recorded as wrong; schema core/STUDY_LOG.md, usually kept in the project's notes vault. Next round: back through you to /study-coach; a new session reads the log first and proposes one topic, its Next up or a weak spot due for review, and any question you bring overrides the plan. Footnote, study-coach hard rule 4: Honest grading: a wrong answer is wrong, here's why, never almost.
svg.title: Scenario 2 — a defense coming up: the deck first, then the rehearsal
svg.desc: You ask results-analyst for verified numbers, science-presenter builds the deck and backup-math slides, and study-coach runs the rehearsal and updates the Study Log; each next round returns through you to study-coach. All three roles are skills in your session; nothing is dispatched.
svg.text: A defense coming up — the deck first, then the rehearsal
